conviction_note: The findings mostly point down, each a small sector or management negative sized on its own (sum -2.2). The scaled number is close to flat (p_up 51 x abs 18 = +0.36) because the bar is very low: spot $4.69 is about 2.4x the annualised midpoint of the company's own Q3 guide, below every sell-side target found, and 52% under the price after the last release. The company has landed its last two non-GAAP guides once the one-off tax item is taken out. The two numbers differ in sign because the sum adds up sector negatives that the price already carries, and p_up weighs them against how low the expectations are. The move will be decided by the Q4 guide, and no source found says which way it goes.

expectations.real_bar: The quarter inside RMB400-500m is the base case. To rise, the release needs a Q4 outlook at or above the Q3 range, with signs that C-M2 or first-payment defaults peaked in Q3, and no further cut to capital return. To fall, it needs a Q4 guide below RMB400m or a dividend or buffer statement that signals more stress.

next_guide.company_current_guide: Q3 2026 only: non-GAAP net income RMB400-500m, net income RMB360-460m. No Q4 guide yet; the company guides one quarter ahead.
next_guide.basis: On the Q2 call management said normalisation of C-M2 'will probably still take at least two to three quarters', volume will not return to Q2 levels soon, funding costs will trend up in H2, and it will take an 'extra cautious approach in business planning for the rest of 2026'. That points to a Q4 guide around the Q3 range rather than a rebound. The Q3 2026 ABS market recovery (CLS, 2026-11-18) is the main thing that could lift it.

findings.finding: Qfin has landed its last two quarterly non-GAAP guides once the one-off is taken out. Q1 2026 was RMB945.9m against a 900-950 guide. Q2 was RMB454.9m against 900-980, with about RMB500m of non-recurring tax charge inside it, so about RMB955m excluding it. The Q3 guide of RMB400-500m was set on 2026-08-25 with July and August data in hand and described as 'extra cautious'. The street's $0.46/ADS is the guide midpoint, so a print in the upper half of the range is the likely outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026, a top-of-guide quarter with a flat Q2 guide: +25.02%. Q2 2026, in line ex-tax but with a halved Q3 guide: -18.91%. The stock has traded the guide, not the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: The street sits at the guide midpoint and the preview frames the risk as a miss. A market pricing the guide record would show a consensus above RMB450m, or a whisper above $0.46. Neither exists. The size is small because the result lands inside what the company already guided.
findings.independence: Q1 actual vs guide: https://finviz.com/news/338117/qfin-holdings-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-unaudited-financial-results-and-raises-semi-annual-dividend (Q1 guide RMB900-950m). Q2 tax one-off: https://news.10jqka.com.cn/20261015/c680748634.shtml. Both are company documents with different dates from the Q2 release.

findings.finding: CEO Haisheng Wu stepped down on 2026-09-20. Chief Risk Officer Yan Zheng (CRO since 2020, 18 years in consumer-finance risk) became CEO effective 2026-09-21, so this is the first print and the first guide under a risk-officer CEO. That raises the chance of heavier Q3 provisioning or a conservative Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-09-21 6-K session in the baseline moved -1.98%, a small reaction to the announcement itself. No prior print under this CEO.
findings.why_not_priced: The announcement was priced as a personnel event (-2%). How a new CEO sets his first guide is only visible tonight. If it were priced, the street would show a Q4 number below the Q3 range, and no Q4 street figure was found. This is an inference about behaviour, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Chinese coverage confirms Wu moves to the international business and Zheng, a risk specialist, takes over: https://news.10jqka.com.cn/20260925/c680282628.shtml and https://wallstreetcn.com/articles/3782228. Same event, different reporters.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call management said: August FPD3/FPD7 up about 20% MoM; August C-M2 guided up about 25% sequentially, with C-M2 up noticeably in Q3; normalisation 'will probably still take at least two to three quarters'; external funding cost up about 25bp in July-August and expected to trend up in H2; volume will not return to Q2 levels soon. That points to a Q4 guide held around the depressed Q3 level, not a recovery.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide line decides this stock: the Q2 2026 guide cut gave -18.91% and the Q1 2026 guide gave +25.02%.
findings.why_not_priced: These statements are public and partly priced, since the stock is down 52% since. What is not settled is whether Q4 is guided flat (relief at 2.4x earnings) or lower (more pain). With no Q4 street number, the market has no anchor. The range is wide and the sign is only slightly negative because management's own timeline puts no recovery in Q4.
findings.independence: The Q3 guide assumptions in the release match the transcript: https://finviz.com/news/385508/qfin-holdings-announces-second-quarter-and-interim-2026-unaudited-financial-results-and-declares-semi-annual-dividend. Same company, different document.

findings.finding: Peers guided Q3 down hard after the same late-June funding shock. LexinFintech expects a significant decrease in Q3 origination and a possible net loss. FinVolution expects China transaction volume to shrink significantly in Q3. Jiayin posted its first interim loss (RMB245m). Lexin's and FinVolution's Q3 2026 releases are not out before QFIN's.
findings.link: Same business model: China online loan facilitation for bank and consumer-finance funding partners, the same bank-funding channel, and the same NFRA facilitation rules (effective 2025-10-01). Five listed facilitators including QFIN, FINV, LX, JFIN and XYF are reported together (Q2 combined volume RMB184.7bn, QFIN RMB63.4bn of it).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No QFIN reaction to a peer read-through measured.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: these are August guides already in the sector's price. It is filed because it confirms that QFIN's Q3 guide was not uniquely pessimistic. If the market thought QFIN's cut was over-done relative to peers, the stock would not have underperformed KWEB by this much.

findings.finding: Lufax reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-27. Its net loss quadrupled to RMB1,494m, the C-M3 flow rate on total loans rose to 1.2% from 1.0% in Q2, and management said it 'exited certain high-risk customer segments'. This shows China consumer-credit quality still deteriorating through Q3.
findings.link: Weak link: both are China consumer/retail credit, but Lufax lends largely to small-business owners through its own consumer-finance balance sheet, a different customer and funding mix. No shared customers stated.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and four weeks old, so it is probably priced in QFIN's November drop. It is filed because it is the only Q3 2026 credit print from a China consumer lender before QFIN. Small because the link is weak.

findings.finding: The China consumer-loan ABS funding channel recovered in Q3 2026. Fitch Bohua puts enterprise-ABS consumer-finance issuance at RMB72.51bn, +20.1% QoQ and +8.8% YoY, and ABN at RMB62.9bn, +11.3% YoY. AAAsf issuance rates were 1.66% (<=1y, -23bp) and 1.78% (1-2y, -19bp), with internet institutions under 2.00%. Internet platforms supplied 84% of Jan-Sep deals. Against this, Lianhe's pool cumulative 90+ default rate rose to 1.01% from end-2025. QFIN guided funding cost +25bp in July-August, so a Q3 that eased into September is upside to funding cost and to the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured reaction on funding-cost surprises. The funding-cost guide was part of the Q2 guide cut that gave -18.91%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an industry series in Chinese, published six days ago, that does not name Qfin. The English previews still quote the company's 'funding costs up 25bp' from August. If it were priced, the preview would frame funding as easing. It is a proxy (market-wide ABS, led by Ant, JD and Tencent), so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Proxy; nothing company-level confirms it. China Daily (2026-10-22) says leading platforms keep funding-cost advantages as small ones exit: https://www.chinadailyhk.com/article/641518.

findings.finding: The buyback has been suspended since late June. The CFO said the priority is to 'weather the storm' and that the company 'may need to build additional financial buffer'. H1 dividend was $0.46/ADS at a ~30% payout, about 10% of today's $4.69 price. Cash and short-term investments were RMB10.6bn (incl. restricted) at 2026-06-30. A buyback resumption tonight is possible but not the base case. The next dividend decision comes with FY results, outside the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The buyback suspension disclosed on the Q2 call was part of the -18.91% session. The Q2 2025 buyback announcement is not in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: The market capitalisation (about $600m) sits below gross cash and short-term investments (about $1.5bn, partly restricted), and convertible notes raised about $677m net. A resumption would be a clear upside surprise that the price does not carry. The CFO's own language makes it unlikely, so the expected value is small and the range is skewed up.
findings.independence: The preview names the buyback as a swing factor: https://finviz.com/news/423403/qfins-profit-floor-faces-its-first-test-as-credit-stress-and-funding-costs-bite. The dividend and cash figures are in the Q2 release (shared document with finding 1).

findings.finding: Expectations are very low. Spot $4.69 is down 52% since the 2026-08-25 release, -17.4% over 20 days and about 5% above the 52-week low. It is below every sell-side target found (Citi Sell $8, JPM Underweight $9, MS Equal Weight $13). The market capitalisation (about 128m ADS x $4.69, roughly $600m) is about 2.4x the annualised midpoint of the company's own Q3 non-GAAP guide (RMB450m, about $63m a quarter). The price already assumes profit falls below the guide, so a quarter in range with a flat Q4 guide clears the real bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 at a depressed price with a guide that held: +25.02%. Q2 2026 after a run with a guide cut: -18.91%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so by definition it is the market's view. What could be mispriced is the gap between a 2.4x multiple on the company's own guide and a guide the company has met twice. If the market trusted the guide, the stock would trade nearer the post-print low ($4.94 cited in the preview) or the $6.83 earnings-AVWAP rather than at a new low into the print. Sized small: being cheap is not a catalyst.

The other baseline rows (-3.01, -1.98, -0.64, +0.96, +0.59, +6.4) are non-earnings 6-Ks: AGM, management change, date notices. The earnings moves are larger than the 15.5% event-implied move.

findings.finding: Independent director Andrew Yan sold about 657k shares on 2026-09-24/25 at $7.36-7.52, plus 850 on 2026-09-29, right after the CEO change. That is the only insider activity found since the Q2 print; the last insider buys were director Eric Chen in March and June 2026 at $12-14.
findings.why_not_priced: Public but obscure (FactSet via HL; HK disclosure). It is a single independent director, not management, so it says little about the quarter. Sized near zero. The price/share basis is unclear (FactSet flags data quality).

findings.finding: Low short interest: 2.8M ADS (about 2% of ADS) and 1.4 days to cover at 2026-09-30. Open interest is call-heavy (put/call 0.07). There is no crowded short to squeeze on good news, and the call open interest may represent existing rebound bets.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning context with no direction of its own. Filed so judges know a squeeze is not a mechanism here.

findings.finding: Regulatory overhang inside the quarter. The comprehensive-financing-cost disclosure rule for personal loans took effect 2026-08-01, with a self-regulatory norm from five associations on 2026-09-18 and online-marketing rules from 2026-09-30. A nationwide campaign against collection agencies cut collection capacity. Draft guidance would push loan cost caps below 24% by 2027. All of this pressures pricing (QFIN average pricing 18.2% in Q2, down from 18.7%) and collection efficiency into Q4 and 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The collection crackdown and the June shock were the stated cause of the Q3 guide cut (-18.91%).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, since the regimes were known before Q3. Filed because the Q4 guide is the first to reflect a full quarter under the August disclosure rule and the September marketing rules. If the market expected no further pricing pressure, the multiple would not sit at 2.4x.

baseline_tension: The baseline gives no skew and a call-heavy open interest (put/call 0.07). The 20-day run-up is -17.4% into the print and the stock is at a 52-week low. The findings lean slightly negative on the sector but cut against a price that already assumes profit below the guide. The tension goes into p_up near 50 rather than into a direction.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside the guided range): guide-track-record finding cut from +1.0 to +0.5, because it lands inside what the company already guided.
Lessons 1/5 and the definition's 'cheap is not a finding': expectations/valuation finding cut from +2.0 to +1.0. A low multiple is not a catalyst, though the v3b addendum keeps it filed.
Untrustworthy FPI history lesson: base rate rebuilt from confirmed releases (-18.91, +25.02, Q4 2025 down); abs_move raised from 17 to 18 on that.
Inside-guide and balanced-evidence lessons moved p_up from 52 to 51.
Lesson 7: short interest checked (about 2%, 1.4 DTC), so no negative was shrunk for squeeze risk. No skew to argue against.
